subject: Onboarding roadmap, commit milestones & latency concessions
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding roadmap, commit milestones & latency concessions

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP_v1_ACME.pdf) that pairs technical eval milestones with commercial triggers so we have a clear, timeboxed path to production. High level:

- 0–2 weeks: Integration & smoke tests (canary traffic, private VPC). No commit.
- Week 3–6: Eval ramp (up to 25k tokens/day). If success criteria met (stability, evaluation metric >= 0.92), customer signs a 3-month initial commit to 75k tokens/day.
- Month 4+: Full ramp to 100k tokens/day and commitment to annual reserved capacity thereafter for predictable unit pricing.

Commercial linkages we propose:
- Pricing: list pricing at 100k/day commit; 10% volume discount is contingent on reaching the Month-4 commit.
- Credits: If Redwood fails to meet the agreed latency SLO during the committed period, customer receives service credits pro-rated to the shortfall.
- Latency SLO: We propose P95 generation latency <= 150ms for the committed tier after ramp. For the eval phase we can offer a best-effort target of P95 <= 200ms.

Open items where we need your confirmation:
1) Acceptance of the MAP milestones and go/no-go criteria (see embedded checklist).
2) Whether procurement needs a different form of SLA credit calculation (we included a simple linear credit table in the attachment).
3) If Acme requires a lower P95 target (e.g., 120ms), we’ll need a higher committed volume (or a modest price increase) to prioritize scheduling on lower-latency pools.

Next steps: If this aligns, can we lock the MAP and aim to sign by 08/31 so procurement can start paperwork? I’ve looped Monica for technical onboarding coordination.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: MAP_v1_ACME.pdf (MAP with milestones, acceptance criteria, and SLA credit table)
From: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@cloudpartner.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding roadmap, commit milestones & latency concessions

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the MAP draft. A few clarifying items from my side:

- Procurement will need a clear SLA credits calculation (they dislike ambiguous "pro-rated" language). Can you convert the linear credit example to a short table showing % credits at P95 bands (e.g., >150ms = 5%, >200ms = 10%)?
- On latency targets: 150ms P95 would be great but our product team expects 120ms for the customer-facing experience. Is the trade you mention (higher commit or price increase) negotiable in the middle (e.g., 90k tokens/day -> 125ms)?
- We also need an example of an evaluation metric pass/fail test — can you share a short test harness or set of prompt/response checks we can run during the 3–6 week eval?

Procurement asked me to flag that DocuSign or a PO-based close is preferred; they will not sign paper. Liam — are there marketplace/partner terms we should consider if Acme routes via your channel?

If possible, can someone from Redwood confirm the credit table and an updated MAP by Monday so we can review with procurement on Tuesday?

Best,
Sara Thomas
Head of Product, Acme Corporation

---
On Sat, Aug 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message attached)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding roadmap, commit milestones & latency concessions

Hi Sara / team —

Looping in from Commercial. Appreciate the clarity on procurement needs. We can do the following concession structure to make the MAP commercially actionable while protecting our capacity planning:

1) Latency vs. commit ladder (finalized):
   - Eval phase (Weeks 0–6): Target P95 <= 200ms (best effort).
   - Initial commit (3 months at 75k tokens/day): P95 <= 150ms. If Acme signs a 6-month initial commit at 90k tokens/day, we will target P95 <= 125ms.

2) Price / discount linkage:
   - Price A (monthly billing): baseline price X.
   - 10% discount applied when Month-4 commit >= 100k tokens/day.
   - 5% upfront contract credit if Acme accepts 6-month 90k/day commit at signing.

3) SLA credits (procurement-friendly table):
   - P95 <= target: 0% credit
   - P95 > target but <= target + 50ms: 5% service credit for affected days
   - P95 > target + 50ms: 10% service credit for affected days
4) Operational guarantees: we will provide a two-week canary window with detailed latency histograms and a dedicated SRE contact during Week 3–6.

Jonas / Monica: please attach the small test harness (a set of ~25 prompts + pass/fail criteria) to the updated MAP and convert the credit table into a single-page appendix for procurement.

Sara — based on this, can Acme confirm whether you prefer the 3-month 75k path (flexible ramp) or the 6-month 90k path (lower latency + upfront credit)? If you sign the 6-month option we will also add a one-time 5% invoice credit at the first billing cycle.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding roadmap, commit milestones & latency concessions

Sara —

Nice to meet you over email. A few operational items to get the MAP over the finish line:

- I attached a redlined MAP (MAP_v1_redline.pdf) that contains the SLA credit table Marissa outlined and a one-page test harness for the eval team.
- We can commit to the 6-month 90k tokens/day path at the following commercial package: 5% upfront invoice credit at first billing + target P95 <= 125ms after ramp. If P95 exceeds the target by more than 50ms, we apply a 10% credit for affected days.
- For procurement: we support DocuSign. If Acme prefers a PO, we can accept a PO + standard SOW; that will push the legal review 2–3 business days but is fine.
- Proposed close timeline: sign MAP + DocuSign by 2026-08-31, start technical onboarding Week of 2026-09-06, canary window Week of 2026-09-13.

Next steps for acme: confirm which commit path you want (3mo/@75k vs 6mo/@90k), and whether DocuSign is acceptable. I’ll provision a dedicated SRE and open the canary slot once we have a signed MAP.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
